Title: WSL working directories rejected with NotCapable permission error
Description: A command cwd inside WSL (e.g. \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\...) reached Deno fs and spawn paths that cannot scope UNC paths, failing with `NotCapable: Requires all access` instead of running. node also misattributes a missing cwd as ENOENT on the binary.
Fix: New resolveCwdForShell(): WSL paths never touch Deno fs or spawn cwd — Ubuntu runs get an explicit `cd '<wsl-path>' &&` prefix with a hidden `test -d` probe; \\host\distro\mnt\<drive> UNCs map back to drive paths for Windows shells; Linux-only paths in Windows shells are refused with a message naming the Ubuntu shell. Missing/unusable cwds now fail fast with actionable messages; residual UNC permission denials map to a clear permission message.
Notes: Covers drive-letter, UNC, absolute WSL and relative inputs; quoteWsl escapes embedded single quotes. Regression tests in shell_test.ts (translation) and runner_test.ts (rejection without spawning).

Title: Console window flashes on every page load and subprocess spawn
Description: Deno.Command on Windows always opens a visible console for console-subsystem binaries and offers no windowsHide option in Deno 2.9.x. The installed-shell probe (where.exe) ran through Deno.Command on every page init, so `deno task dev` constantly flashed auto open/close terminal windows; same flash on pickFolder/pickFile (powershell.exe) and cancelRun (taskkill).
Fix: Replaced all runtime spawns with node:child_process honoring windowsHide:true (CREATE_NO_WINDOW): spawnSync for quick probes (where.exe, taskkill) and async spawn for the PowerShell picker dialogs — the Compressy pattern (bindings.ts/vips.ts). explorer.exe deliberately keeps NO windowsHide (it would suppress Explorer's own window, probe-verified in Compressy).
Notes: Build scripts (scripts/*.ts) and tests still use Deno.Command — harmless in a terminal context. Regression rule: any new Deno.Command of a console binary in app runtime reintroduces flashing; use node:child_process + windowsHide instead. Upstream gap: denoland/deno#34627 (Deno.Command lacks windowsHide).

Title: Blank window on Windows with the webview backend
Description: Webview backend shows a blank window on Win11 (denoland/deno#35645); WebView2 additionally sanitizes input[type=file] paths, hiding absolute paths from the app.
Fix: Pinned backend cef in deno.json and every desktop task; folder picking stays Deno-side (bindings.pickFolder via FolderBrowserDialog) for the same reason.
Notes: Switch back only after the upstream fix ships stable plus a smoke test.

Title: Event prefix split-brain: standalone input-* tags emit input:* while <e-input> emits e:*
Description: A listener written for one prefix is silently deaf to the other; the single highest-impact open defect in the library audit sheet.
Fix: App uses <e-input type=...> exclusively and subscribes to e:* only; never bundles or references the input-* tags. registry.ts widgetToEInput bridges the 30-token grammar to the element types.
Notes: Upstream: enhanced-inputs/sheets/report.csv (event-prefix rows); library fix tracked as EI2.

Title: Combobox/select dropdowns missing ARIA relationships
Description: No aria-activedescendant, aria-controls or aria-multiselectable on the select/combobox/radio/checkbox-group listboxes; unassociated for screen readers.
Fix: Accepted for v1; keyboard operation still works. Logged here per plan section 4.14.
Notes: Upstream: enhanced-inputs/sheets/report.csv rows L44/L45/L46; library fix tracked as EI4.

Title: Undeclared wc-datepicker dependency for the date picker
Description: Demos load <wc-datepicker> from a CDN but it is in neither package.json nor src/ imports; the picker slot is inert.
Fix: Ship without the picker; the native date input works via the _getInputType mapping. No app code depends on the picker.
Notes: Adopting it would break offline; dependency would need vendoring like range-slider-element.

Title: Unstyled shadow mode renders unreachable elements
Description: createRenderRoot attaches a shadow root when the shadow attribute is set, but no shadow-scoped styles and no part hooks exist anywhere in the library; the element renders completely unstyled and unreachable by theme CSS.
Fix: Never set the shadow attribute; light DOM only.
Notes: Styling contract is .i-* classes plus --input-* tokens (default.css vendored into static/vendor/).

Title: Readme documents .e-* classes that do not exist
Description: Documented .e-wrapper/.e-label/.e-input/.e-description/.e-error classes have zero matches in src/, themes or demos; the e- names come from generated element IDs (_generateIds), not CSS.
Fix: Style .i-* classes only; never trust the readme CSS section.
Notes: Same rewrite should fix the zero-dependencies claim, the zod-mini claim, the components/e-input.js subpath and the aspirational WCAG claim. Tracked as EI5.

Title: internals.setValidity anchor TypeError on invalid fields
Description: The invalid branch calls internals.setValidity with a non-HTMLElement anchor, throwing TypeError and rejecting validate(); verified in Chrome via Playwright on an empty required text field.
Fix: App disables automatic validation (validate-on empty), validates explicitly through safeValidate() with caught rejections, and filters that exact rejection message in an unhandledrejection handler. Console stays clean.
Notes: Discovered during E7 verification; candidate for the library audit sheet.

Title: e:validate fires before validity is computed
Description: Async validate() dispatches e:validate first, so detail.valid is stale at dispatch time; verified: an empty required field reports valid true in the event while el.valid ends false.
Fix: App re-reads element state (quickCheck for gating) instead of trusting detail.valid; e:success/e:error are observed as well.

Title: Unknown action-button values render no button, so no browse affordance
Description: _renderAction falls through to an empty string for unrecognized values, so action-button=browse (assumed by app spec section 4.7) is inert.
Fix: Host renders its own Browse button beside file widgets, wired to bindings.pickFile/pickFolder.
Notes: Verified in source; no upstream change needed unless the library adopts a browse contract.

Title: Re-running a command reuses the same terminal session instead of starting a new one
Description: Each run targets the same per-card .term-body: runFlow() calls termReset() which disposes the xterm instance and clears the element, so the previous run output is destroyed when a command re-runs. Backend enforces the same model with a single ActiveRun/lastCompleted — a second run while one is active is rejected with 'a command is already running'. No per-run session id, no run history; writeRunInput/cancelRun/__ccActiveTerm address only the single active run.
Fix: Decide session model: either append a new terminal session per run (run-id keyed bodies, history list, per-session cancel/input/close-guard wiring) or keep single-session but preserve last output (e.g. confirm before discarding). Parallel sessions need a run registry keyed by id instead of single active/lastCompleted.
Notes: K2 deliberately built fresh-instance-per-run (termReset comment); this bug asks to revisit that decision. Repro: run any command, run it again — first output is wiped. Related: G2 close guard assumes one live terminal.
